isabel: New hire blocked on the Workers quickstart. Deploy throws: "ReferenceError: process is not defined" then a runtime error for "net". We only use fetch + jwt verify. Any short fixes?

ravi: Usually a transitive dep is pulling node builtins (buffer/net/fs). Which jwt lib?

isabel: Using jwt-helper-lite. Bundle shows buffer pulled in by a base64 helper.

sam: Two immediate options: 1) swap to a web-first JWT verify (use WebCrypto directly), or 2) add an explicit small shim package that exports web-safe helpers and opt-in stubs for node builtins.

sam: For publish pattern we prefer conditional exports so bundlers pick worker entrypoints: 
```json
{"exports": {"./verify": {"worker": "dist/verify.worker.mjs", "node": "dist/verify.node.cjs"}}, "types":"dist/index.d.ts"}
```
This prevents node-only code from being bundled into worker builds if the bundler respects conditional exports.

ravi: Also watch for deep imports like `jwt-helper/lib/codec` — conditional exports only protect top-level entrypoints. We should audit samples and update imports to top-level public API. Add a CI lint check to fail on deep imports.

isabel: WebCrypto differences too — CF Workers might lack some subtle.importKey behaviors for certain key formats. What's our guidance?

sam: Provide a runtime guard in the shim with a clear error linking to docs. Example: `if (typeof crypto?.subtle?.importKey !== 'function') throw Error('WebCrypto importKey not available; see devex guide')`. For critical flows recommend server-side verification fallback or WASM verifier.

ravi: Auth/retry nuance: Workers can't use long-lived sockets. Token refresh must be guarded to avoid parallel refresh storms. Pattern: store the refresh Promise on globalThis and reuse it. Single refresh attempt, then up to 2 exponential backoffs for other transient failures.

isabel: TS consumers hit "Cannot find module '@redwood/inference-edge-shims'" when we prototype the shim. How to fix types?

sam: Ship `index.d.ts` and set `types` in package.json. Also include a README snippet for sample tsconfig: `{"lib":["es2021","webworker"],"moduleResolution":"bundler","skipLibCheck":true}`. That avoids DOM/Node type collisions.

ravi: CI note: current integration runner executes worker tests in plain node and fails due to missing WebCrypto. Add a Miniflare job to the matrix and mark tests accordingly.

devx-bot: Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/620 - adds `@redwood/inference-edge-shims` (mjs/cjs/worker builds) + d.ts and updates samples. CI still needs miniflare job.

ci-bot: Created ticket CI-1456 to add Miniflare run for worker-target tests.

isabel: Thanks. If we ship a tiny official shim and update the quickstart with a short checklist (node builtins, webcrypto caveats, bundler target flags, tsconfig), new hires should stop hitting this.

sam: Agreed. I'll add the lint rule to warn about node-only imports when package indicates platform: worker and update the sample imports to use the shim.

isabel: Perfect, that should smooth onboarding. :raised_hands:
